response: No, gestational age misclassification does not fully explain the difference in birthweights between Australian Aborigines and whites. Studies have shown that even after adjusting for gestational age, birthweights of Australian Aboriginal infants are generally lower than those of non-Aboriginal infants. This suggests that other factors, such as socioeconomic disadvantage, poor maternal health, and limited access to healthcare, contribute to the difference in birthweights between these populations.
